about: Inputs for bidprice.html. An invented hub network at Montréal (YUL): two feeder legs in, two long-haul legs out, eight itineraries, three fare classes. Every fare, demand figure and capacity is an illustrative assumption, not any airline's data. Fares are one-way economy fares in Canadian dollars.

presets.label: Busy hub
presets.blurb: Every leg is in demand. Connecting passengers pay less than the local long-haul fare in the same class, as they often do in markets where they could connect elsewhere.

presets.label: Too much connecting traffic
presets.blurb: The long-haul flights are the bottleneck and the feeders have room. Lots of cheap connecting demand books in the same classes as local passengers, so leg-based control can't tell them apart and lets too many in.

presets.label: Full feeders, room on long-haul
presets.blurb: The small feeder aircraft are the bottleneck and the long-haul flights have spare seats. Leg-based control sees only a small prorated slice of a connecting fare on the feeder and turns away passengers worth far more to the network.
